title: Cohomology of the dual of a finite complex over a field
statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $C$ be a bounded complex of finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces, and let $C^\vee =R\operatorname {Hom}_E(C,E)$. The canonical evaluation $C\otimes _E^LC^\vee \to E$ induces perfect pairings

$$
H^i(C)\times H^{-i}(C^\vee )\longrightarrow E \qquad (i\in \mathbf Z),
$$

and the canonical comparison $C\to C^{\vee \vee }$ is an isomorphism; equivalently

$$
H^{-i}(C^\vee )\xrightarrow {\  \sim \  }H^i(C)^\vee \qquad (i\in \mathbf Z).
$$

proof.text: Write $Z^j=\ker d_C^j$, $B^j=\operatorname{im}d_C^{j-1}$ and $V^j=Z^j/B^j=H^j(C)$, using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Every vector space is projective by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective]. Its lifting property in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], applied to the identity maps of $B^{j+1}$ and $V^j$, gives sections $s_j:B^{j+1}\to C^j$ of $d_C^j:C^j\twoheadrightarrow B^{j+1}$ and $t_j:V^j\to Z^j$ of the quotient. Put $L^j=s_j(B^{j+1})$ and $W^j=t_j(V^j)$. Then $C^j=B^j\oplus W^j\oplus L^j$: subtract $s_j(d_Cx)$ to enter $Z^j$, then subtract $t_j$ of its quotient class to enter $B^j$; applying $d_C$ and then the quotient also proves uniqueness. The only nonzero differential block is the isomorphism $d_C:L^j\to B^{j+1}$. The projection $C^j\twoheadrightarrow W^j$ sends a finite spanning set to a finite spanning set, so $W^j$, hence $V^j$, is finite dimensional by [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. All these summands vanish outside the finite support of $C$.

proof.text: Let $H$ be the complex with $H^j=W^j$ and zero differential. The inclusion $a:H\to C$ and projection $b:C\to H$ are chain maps with $ba=1_H$. On the complementary complex $T^j=B^j\oplus L^j$, define $h^j:T^j\to T^{j-1}$ to be $(d_C:L^{j-1}\to B^j)^{-1}$ on $B^j$ and zero on $L^j$. Then $dh+hd=1_T$: $dh$ is the identity on the $B$ block and $hd$ on the $L$ block. Extend $h$ by zero on $H$. Thus $1_C-ab=dh+hd$, so $a,b$ are inverse in the homotopy category and therefore in its derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This is precisely $C\cong\bigoplus_jH^j(C)[-j]$; the sum is finite. The induced identification $W^j\cong H^j(C)$ is the original cycle quotient, not a newly chosen cohomology identification.

source.place: Proof, Steps 1–3; expanded splitting and evaluation calculation. Compare current main-20261015 unit sk-thm-derived-duality, its sole proof paragraph.

proof.text: The terms of $H$ are projective by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective] and $H$ is bounded. Apply [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model] to $P=H$ and $N=E[0]$. It gives a representative $D=\operatorname{Hom}_E^\bullet(H,E[0])$ of $H^\vee$, together with the representative of its actual derived evaluation. In degree $q$ only the factor with input degree $-q$ survives, so $D^q=\operatorname{Hom}_E(W^{-q},E)$. Its differential is zero because both differentials in the Hom formula are zero. Consequently $H^{-i}(H^\vee)=\operatorname{Hom}_E(W^i,E)$. The evaluation on $W^i\otimes D^{-i}$ is $x\otimes\phi\mapsto(-1)^{i(-i)}\phi(x)=(-1)^i\phi(x)$. This sign comes from the order $H\otimes H^\vee$ in the stated evaluation; it is an invertible scalar.

source.place: Proof, Steps 1–3; expanded splitting and evaluation calculation. Compare current main-20261015 unit sk-thm-derived-duality, its sole proof paragraph.

proof.text: The comparison of the preceding step is natural. For $a:H\to C$, the dual map $a^\vee:C^\vee\to H^\vee$ is precomposition with $a$. Naturality of the evaluation counit gives $\operatorname{ev}_C\circ(a\otimes1)=\operatorname{ev}_H\circ(1\otimes a^\vee)$. Both $a$ and $a^\vee$ are isomorphisms in $D(E)$, so applying cohomology identifies the pairing in the statement with $(x,\phi)\mapsto(-1)^i\phi(x)$ on $W^i\times(W^i)^\vee$. Here the product of cohomology classes is represented by the tensor of their cycle representatives, by the total tensor model of [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model]. For a finite basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $W^i$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], let $e_1^*,\ldots,e_r^*$ be its coordinate functionals. Every functional is uniquely $\sum_t\phi(e_t)e_t^*$, so these form a basis of the dual, and the pairing matrix is $(-1)^i I_r$. Its inverse is the same matrix. Thus both adjoints of the pairing are bijections: this proves perfectness and identifies the canonical map $H^{-i}(C^\vee)\to H^i(C)^\vee$ as an isomorphism. Splittings were used to verify the canonical map; the map itself is defined by evaluation and uses no choices.

source.place: Proof, Steps 1–3; expanded splitting and evaluation calculation. Compare current main-20261015 unit sk-thm-derived-duality, its sole proof paragraph.

proof.text: The given bounded finite-dimensional complex has finite projective terms, by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective] and the finite spanning condition, and hence is a perfect point complex by [def-pod-perfect-point-complex]. Apply [prop-pod-biduality-at-the-point] to this $C$ at coefficient ring $E$. Its first conclusion is exactly that the canonical comparison $C\to C^{\vee\vee}$, defined by evaluation and coevaluation, is an isomorphism. Together with Step 4 this proves all clauses of the item.
